figures.caption: Fig. 1: Overview of the proposed multi-scale temporal framework, illustrated with the {full, 2, 10} configuration. The 18-channel EEG signal of length 6000 samples is decomposed into three temporal scales: one full-signal window (18×6000), two 10-second windows (18 × 3000 each), and ten 2-second windows (18 × 600 each), for a total of N = 13 windows. All windows are processed by the same shared encoder into 32-dimensional embeddings e1, . . . , e13. The embeddings are integrated by the dynamic fusion module into a single sample-level representation E ∈ R416, which is passed to the classification head.
TABLE II: Two-class classification performance (positive vs. negative) across all window configurations and fusion strategies.

Fig. 2: Test accuracy versus computational cost across all 15 window configurations under dynamic fusion, for the two-class task (a) and the three-class task (b). Each marker denotes a single window configuration; the peak-accuracy configuration in each task is highlighted. The dashed horizontal line marks the full-signal baseline. The peak configurations, {full, 2, 10} for the two-class task and {2, 5, 10} for the three-class task, remain below the maximum-cost four-scale setting, although both lie toward the upper end of the evaluated computational range.
